A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same normalcy-score study. All pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite substantial reformatting. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations, injected-anomaly benchmark experiments, sensitivity analyses and clinical aortic-diameter results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and clinical results and adds Yacht experiments, comparison methods, abstention results and clinical exceedance probabilities.

M1.justification: The two-GP heteroscedastic model, NS definition, expected-score calculation, sparse approximation and sampled HDI construction remain unchanged. Joint training and optimizer assignments receive additional explanation. NShom is introduced as an evaluation control, and clinical exceedance probabilities summarize the existing posterior.

E1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.4 add Yacht Hydrodynamics, covering resistance conditioned on hull geometry and operating conditions. The medical dataset description removes 115 Marfan patients, and the stated clinical test population narrows from adults with Marfan or bicuspid aortic valve to bicuspid patients only. Other dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds Altman's linear variance-estimation method and the single-GP homoscedastic NShom control to the retained benchmark comparisons. These substantively strengthen comparisons concerning heteroscedasticity and regression modeling; Altman was previously discussed but not evaluated. Table 3 additionally compares HDI-based abstention with contextual Isolation Forest abstention.

E3.justification: Precision@n is removed from benchmark evaluation. The new abstention experiment rejects 5% of test instances and computes AUCs on the retained 95%. Five-fold cross-validation, anomaly-injection ranges and the stated training budget remain unchanged. Injection before splitting is newly clarified, without establishing a changed procedure.

E4.justification: v2 adds a homoscedasticity ablation and a direct assessment of HDI-guided abstention, testing central aspects of the approach. Clinical cases gain exceedance-probability analysis. Conversely, v1's HDI-distribution plots and cohort-wide Z-score/NS disagreement analysis disappear, and six illustrated patients become four. The kernel and inducing-point sensitivity studies are retained, merely relabeled as RQ2.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 newly reports posterior probabilities P(NS > 2) alongside patient HDIs, extending uncertainty reporting. Both versions already report five anomaly-injection runs with different seeds, means and standard deviations in Table 2, and clinical DeLong tests. There is no documented increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Substantial result entries are added for Altman, NShom, Yacht and abstention. For example, Yacht NS achieves ROC AUC 0.97 ± 0.02 and PR AUC 0.88 ± 0.06; the abstention comparison reports Concrete PR AUC 0.65 versus 0.55. New clinical counts identify 82 SoV and 48 AA cases with E[NS] < 2 but P(NS > 2) > 0. Precision@n and several diagnostic results are removed. All 56 shared benchmark AUC mean/SD pairs remain unchanged, as do the clinical ROC plots despite the revised cohort description.

T1.justification: The GP definitions, NS formula, log-normal expectation, computational complexity and weighted Kendall-tau expression are mathematically unchanged. The added uncertainty paragraph explains existing expressions and posterior concentration; it supplies no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain their claims about uncertainty-aware CAD and competitive detection performance. The conclusion newly emphasizes the competitiveness of ordinary Z-scores, claims priority for revealing this benchmark finding, and acknowledges that NS sometimes offers only a modest improvement.

C2.justification: v2 expands the interpretation of the log-normal correction and shrinking posterior uncertainty, and attributes non-contextual detectors' disadvantage to the joint-versus-conditional formulation. It clarifies that the 40 mm threshold defines clinical labels only, corrects the heatmap interpretation from AU to EU, and replaces the instruction to discard threshold-straddling cases with quantified exceedance probabilities.

D1.justification: New disclosures specify optimizer responsibilities, injection before train/test splitting, linear-regression Z-score fitting and residual-scale estimation, and use of the original QCAD hyperparameter settings. Training times are newly attributed to an NVIDIA A6000 GPU. Existing kernel, learning rates, inducing-point initialization, epoch limit and software-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Depeweg et al., Le et al., the Yacht dataset, and Heaukulani and van der Wilk. It links joint HGPR training to Le et al. and extends future multivariate modeling discussion to Wishart processes. The new Z-score benchmarking-priority claim modestly changes positioning; the main related-work account remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the abstract, introduction and related work are retained. Local revisions add a training summary, expand uncertainty explanations, rewrite results discussion, promote existing sensitivity analysis to a numbered research question, and add acknowledgments and publication information.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column journal layout. Table 2 is transposed and reorganized, an abstention table is added, and v1 Figures 2 and 5 are removed. Patient panels are reorganized and annotated with probabilities; retained simulation, ROC and heatmap figures are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: The added homoscedastic and Altman controls, direct abstention comparison, and implementation clarifications strengthen empirical support and transparency. These gains are tempered by removal of Precision@n and diagnostic analyses and narrower reported clinical coverage. The unchanged clinical ROC plots despite the revised cohort description also leave rerun status unresolved. Overall, v2 provides a useful but limited strengthening of the paper.
